column1: I think you'll get more useful help if you take a few steps back, and ask us what scientific question  you are trying to answer. Why are you looking for the smallest normalized SD?
No one will be able to answer this without more detail. If you show the calculation that leads to the answer of 35%, we'll will be able to help you understand what that means.

1. You might want to change "STD" to "SD" which is more standard and STD had another meaning (to medical people, STD means sexually transmitted disease).
2. Your final equation isn't quite right. The multiplier is not 1.96 but rather is a constant from the t distribution. With large n, it is 1.96 but with smaller n that multiplier is larger.
